title: Marvel's Rocket, Groot and Howard the Duck Show How Voice Acting Works
excerpt:
Bradley Cooper, Vin Diesel and Seth Green lend voices to beloved digital Marvel characters.
On-set performers and animation teams help bring those characters to life.
body_md:
Some of the Marvel Cinematic Universe's most recognizable characters are created through a collaboration between voice actors, physical performers and visual-effects artists. The face audiences see on screen does not necessarily belong to the performer they hear. A new retrospective highlights Rocket Raccoon, Groot and Howard the Duck as three notable examples of that production approach.

Bradley Cooper voices Rocket Raccoon in the Guardians of the Galaxy films. Rocket's abrasive humor, vulnerability and emotional development rely heavily on Cooper's vocal performance, but Cooper did not physically portray the character on the Guardians sets. Sean Gunn, the director's brother, performed Rocket's movements and interactions during filming, providing the other actors and animation artists with a reference for the digital character.

Vin Diesel supplies the voice of Groot, whose apparently limited vocabulary is built around variations of I am Groot. Director James Gunn has explained that Diesel received special scripts indicating what Groot's words actually meant in each scene. This helped the actor deliver different intentions and emotions even when the spoken phrase remained nearly identical.

Groot's physical references have also changed across productions. Krystian Godlewski performed the role on set for the first Guardians film, Terry Notary contributed to Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame, and Austin Freeman provided on-set work for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3. Gunn has confirmed that neither Cooper nor Diesel had appeared on a Guardians set in the course of providing their respective voices.

Seth Green is another example through his work as Howard the Duck. The sarcastic digital character first appeared in the post-credits sequence of the original Guardians of the Galaxy and later returned in other Marvel projects, including the third Guardians movie. Green contributes Howard's personality through his voice rather than physically portraying an anthropomorphic duck. The retrospective, however, notes that there is less definitive evidence for the broader claim that Green has never visited any Marvel set.

These examples illustrate how modern superhero filmmaking can divide a single screen performance among several contributors. A star's recorded voice, another performer's movement and an animation team's detailed work can combine into a character audiences experience as one coherent personality. This is a behind-the-scenes feature, not an announcement of new casting or upcoming Marvel projects.
seo_title: How Marvel Brought Rocket, Groot and Howard to Life
